newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close at record high after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close at record high after U.S. data.

text.p: French stocks rose to a record closing high on Tuesday, boosted by market-friendly U.S. economic data which lowered fears of a U.S. interest rate hike and lifted debt markets in the United States and Europe.
The dollar's continued strong performance against European currencies also helped the bourse, dealers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 47.59 points or 1.95 percent at 2,482.76, breaking the old record of 2,461.25 set on January 23.
Volume was a heavy 8.95 billion francs.
The release of the U.S. employment cost index for the fourth quarter, which showed the cost of labour rose a smaller than expected 0.8 percent, was the main cause for the bourse's rise, dealers said.

The slightly weaker-than-expected index showed labor cost, a key determinant of inflation in the United States, was not in danger of getting out of control and lessened the chance of a rise in U.S. rates, they said.
The market's eyes will now turn to U.S. durable goods data for December, due on Wednesday.
Moulinex ended 8.52 percent higher at 142.60 francs after earlier being suspended limit up. The share rose after the company predicted improved operating earnings.
Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux both rose as rumours of a linkup, last floated in 1995, resurfaced. Suez also gained from saying on Monday it would post a 1996 profit.
Suez ended the day 6.94 percent higher at 248 francs and Lyonnaise finished 5.05 percent higher at 562 francs.
"Considered several times and regularly postponed, the last time in 1995, this operation is once again under review," daily Le Figaro said, citing sources close to the affair.
Suez and Lyonnaise spokeswomen said the groups' policy was not to comment on "rumours". Suez said on Monday it would earn net profit of about 800 million francs in 1996.

Elf Aquitaine and 55-percent owned unit Sanofi both closed higher after a source close to the company said Sanofi was seeking one or two partners to double its size and help it meet development costs.
Sanofi ended 3.48 percent higher at 565 francs while Elf was up 5.46 percent at 541 france.

Bic closed up 1.37 percent at 891 francs, Valeo ended up 3.24 percent at 363.50 francs and AGF finished 4.83 percent ore 173.80 francs higher, all due to being named members of CAC-40 index, replacing UAP, Eurotunnel and Saint-Louis.
